metadata.scenario_context: Mike, Kim, and Emily, who are university students and schoolmates, have recently partnered to start a company that has just secured a significant investment. They are preparing to celebrate. Recent news indicates that the government is introducing new policies to assist businesses, which they are planning to discuss.

cultural_axis.agent_1_value: People from China have a great deal of confidence in the press at all.
cultural_axis.agent_2_value: People from Australia have no confidence in the press at all.

agent_1.goal_1: Discuss going to a barbecue buffet.
agent_1.goal_2: Question whether  there is confidence in the press.

agent_2.goal_2: Discuss whether there is confidence in the press.

shared_prefix.speaker: Mike
shared_prefix.message:
Hey Kim, I was thinking... we should celebrate our investment with a barbecue buffet. What do you think? 

And, by the way, I've been reading about the government policies to assist businesses. Do you think there's real confidence in the press about those changes?
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Kim
shared_prefix.message:
A barbecue buffet sounds pretty good. I like that idea. It'll be fun. 

About the press... honestly, I have zero confidence in the press at all. They often just twist things around. It’s hard to trust what they say, especially about government policies. I don’t think we can rely on their perspective.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Mike
shared_prefix.message: I get what you're saying, Kim. But, you know, deep down, we are all the same. It's natural to feel skeptical about the press; I think everyone questions reliability at some point. People are pretty much motivated by the same things, wanting to get the truth out there. When you really get to know people, they're pretty much like us. So, while I see your point, I still believe there’s value in trusting some information from the press about these policies. Let's focus on our barbecue plans!
shared_prefix.label: Minimization
